To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) people are more likely to judge that spaced information will be recalled than massed information when they are told that spaced information is better to study than massed information, 2) this effect is stronger for participants who are told that spaced and massed information are equally effective to study, and 3) participants are more likely to make this judgment if they are told to study the spaced and massed lists in different study sessions.
